To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the voltage sags are affected by the DG units connected to the transmission network.
the voltage sag behaviour in transmission systems can be significantly altered by DG units.
the voltage sag behaviour is strongly influenced by the penetration level of DG units and by the location of DG units in the network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the penetration of DG units on the transmission systems.

the voltage sag performance in the transmission system and the effects of DG units on this performance, and we propose a new graphical visualization method that is a powerful tool for the analysis of the voltage sag behaviour in transmission systems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, when DG units are present in the network, the voltage sags are more frequent and more severe than in a transmission system without DG units.
, when the DG is connected to the network, the voltage sags in transmission systems are not only caused by short circuits but are also caused by the short circuits of the DG.
, when a large DG unit is installed in a transmission network, the voltage sag propagation is not affected by the presence of the DG unit.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of DG units can significantly affect the performance of the system in terms of voltage sag.
the DG units connected to the transmission systems by means of HV/MV stations have a significant effect on the propagation of the voltage sags, and this effect can be quantified by the DFV matrix.
the voltage sags in transmission systems are strongly dependent on the fault position, the DG location, and the DG penetration level.
